shortName: Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania
usCourseworkText: Note: This School has progressed to a competency-based admissions process.
additionalCoursework: Perelman School of Medicine (PSOM) does not require any course prerequisites for admission to the school. PSOM seeks students with a broad educational background and rigorous science preparation. Admissions competencies are not based on specific courses, but rather on the cumulative achievement of knowledge and skills needed to become a physician. All applicants must have at minimum, a bachelor's degree prior to matriculation at PSOM.

medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A Leave of Absence can be granted for up to one year by the Associate Dean of Student Affairs with corroboration from the Student Standards Committee. The process for requesting a LOA is outlined under the Academic Performance and Progression Policy on the Student Portal (http://www.med.upenn.edu/student ). During a LOA students are not enrolled in the School of Medicine and activities pursued during this time will not fulfill any M.D., degree requirements.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There is a strong commitment to student life with over 100 official organizations and activities for students in a variety of areas: clinics in underserved areas, varied interest groups, service, outreach and advocacy, interdisciplinary pursuits in medicine, and recreation and well-being.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Penn's urban campus is located in Philadelphia, one of America's most historic and livable cities. The fact that all 12 of Penn's graduate schools are located within walking distance of one another supports and fosters Penn's interdisciplinary approach to education, scholarship, and research. The city is a vibrant cultural center of urban life.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Housing is affordable and there are Campus resources that help students find housing, both in West Philadelphia, Center City, and surrounding areas.  University transit service is available within certain established boundaries.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Penn Med Pride is one of the interest groups available at Perelman. PSOM's lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer student and student allies organization. Our group of LGBTQ students and allies is committed to increasing visibility of LGBTQ people at PSOM; educating the PSOM community about LGBTQ health best practices through a speaker series and curriculum development; promoting LGBTQ health-related community outreach; providing opportunities for professional development; and cultivating our vibrant community of LGBTQ students, faculty, staff, and allies at the Perelman School of Medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Available to students are: 1) faculty/staff for scheduled or walk-in appointments for advising and counseling; 2) the support of student-led spiritual and religious groups; 3) the support of other student-led affinity groups; and 4) a student-led wellness committee along with wellness activities and programming supported by the Office of Student Affairs (including an MS1 hiking retreat, mindfulness and medical humanities electives, and community conversations and dinners). 
 
Academic support programs include test-taking skills, testing accommodations, clinical coaching, and clerkship transition activities. Curricular programs include Doctoring courses and wellness and professionalism lectures. 
 
Students are assigned to learning teams and one of four Houses at matriculation for peer-to-peer support and mentoring. They also have membership to university gyms and participate in student-led sports.  
 
Mental Health services are available through Student Health and Counseling and include on-site/virtual support from two counselors dedicated to medical students. Additional services are available from our special providers including, short-term individual therapy, one-time consultation, connection and referrals to long-term therapy and other resources.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The Perelman School of Medicine (PSOM) cultivates an environment of “rigor with compassion.” This means that standards are set high for academic and professional performance because of the privilege and responsibilities that students have in future endeavors.  This rigorous environment is created with empathy, compassion, and support and that the school’s goal is to ensure success by providing exceptional educational experiences and professional development while nurturing personal wellness.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: No specific dress code but professional dress (white coat) required in patient care setting.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Advising is available at all times: peer tutors, academic resilience, counseling & wellness initiatives. Academic support thru Weingarten Learning Center. All students are assigned an Advisory Dean.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: During the first week of school in both required courses and volunteer clinics.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Integrated basic and clinical sciences, facilitated team-based learning, small group case-based studies, and individualized curriculum opportunities based on career goals.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinic Rotations begin in January of Year 2.  Five major teaching hospitals within walking distance of the School.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Perelman School of Medicine enjoys an international reputation for innovation in areas ranging from leadership training to global health. Our groundbreaking curriculum sets a new standard for medical education nationwide.

The three core blocks of the MD curriculum integrate basic sciences and clinical experience from day one. It teaches students self-directed lifelong learning skills, interdisciplinary teamwork and technological proficiency in the practice of evidence-based medicine and patient-centered care.

Integrated
The IMPaCT curriculum provides integration of basic, translational, social, clinical, and health systems sciences throughout the continuum of medical education, led by outstanding faculty committed to the privilege of teaching tomorrow’s health care leaders.

Innovative
The IMPaCT curriculum provides training designed to enable students to learn and work in teams throughout medical school. Our massive university campus provides unparalleled proximity and access to opportunities for educational enrichment at any of our leading graduate schools, innovative research centers, and renowned clinical facilities.

Individualized
The IMPaCT curriculum provides numerous, diverse opportunities for customization of the medical education journey and the pursuit of unique professional experiences so that all specific interests and career goals can be attained.

The curriculum emphasizes self-directed lifelong learning and small-group instruction. The Henry A. Jordan Medical Education Center itself plays a prominent role in the training of future physicians and scientists; it is among the first medical education spaces in the nation physically integrated into active clinical and research facilities.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Penn is an outstanding institution for research. Ranked among the top in the nation in NIH funding, there are well over 500 faculty members conducting basic and clinical research. Penn students tap into these resources in a number of ways: short-term elective research, scholarly pursuit, year-out programs with funding, a top MD/PhD program, and research-oriented MD/Masters programs. Read more about these opportunities at the following website: https://www.med.upenn.edu/admissions/dual-degrees.html
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Three-month scholarly pursuit and/or dual degree.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Clinical education occurs at the following owned and affiliated hospitals: University of Pennsylvania Health System, Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, and VA Philadelphia Medical Center
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: See curriculum description where grades for each core are noted.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: As the nation's first medical school and home to the first teaching hospital, the Perelman School of Medicine has a long tradition of academic excellence and scientific discovery. Building on this tradition, our innovative, interdisciplinary research programs continue today to pave the way for a future of new paradigms in cutting-edge science. As an internationally renowned community of scientists and physicians, we are dedicated to both advancing knowledge and fostering a culture of excellence in training the next generation of scientific leaders. Our faculty are at the forefront of the biomedical revolution, and we are committed to sustaining a vibrant intellectual environment, with the ultimate goal of translating ground-breaking discoveries into medical therapies that will eradicate disease and improve health care around the world.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania will select students who are poised and prepared to become future physician leaders in health care. These students will serve their communities and contribute to society through their clinical, educational, research, health policy, and entrepreneurial efforts. Graduates of the Perelman School of Medicine will seek to advance care quality, science and discovery for the benefit of their local communities and the field of medicine more broadly. We strive to develop a highly talented student body with a breadth of personal and professional experiences that reflect these goals.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: All letters must be signed and on official stationery. The Perelman School of Medicine has no maximum for letters of recommendation, however, applicants may only submit up to 10 letters through the AMCAS Letter Writer Application. Additional letters of recommendation or personal updates to the application can be added to an application at any time. The applicant can upload any updates directly into the application using the online status page. Applicants who have previously applied for admission to the School of Medicine must resubmit the required letters of recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Composite or committee: Individual letter/letter packet from a pre-health advisor or career service office, with or without additional letters attached.
- OR -
A minimum of three (3) letters from faculty members who know the applicant well; at least one must come from a science faculty member with whom the applicant has taken courses.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interview day activities include orientation, meeting students, financial aid discussion, and curriculum interaction.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Applicants must meet the mean GPA and MCAT of the entering class and be pre-approved by the Committee on Admissions before submitting.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Must have completed 24 credits of science education (BCPM credits) in the US before applying; limited funding for non-US citizens
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Please visit our admissions website at www.med.upenn.edu/admissions for any updates regarding policies or any changes to the timeline for admission.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college credits are considered on a case-by-case basis. The committee will take into account the reasons for completion, such as financial considerations, academic scheduling, and geographic limitations, as well as whether additional upper division courses/labs were taken at a 4-year institution or post-baccalaureate program.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicant updates, letters of continued interest, grade updates, and publication updates should be submitted by the applicant through the portal. All files must be under 4MB in size.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Please see the Technical Standards website for detailed information.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Students come from all social, economic, and cultural backgrounds. Financial aid includes need-based scholarships and federal loans for accepted students that apply via the CSS Profile. Only US citizens and permanent residents are eligible for federal loans. The school also provides approximately 35 full-tuition & fee merit scholarships awarded to each new accepted class regardless of citizenship.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Student selection is a multifactorial process that is guided by our school’s mission to prepare future physician leaders who will serve society through their clinical, educational, research, health policy, and entrepreneurial efforts. Our review process emphasizes individualized review to evaluate competencies, attributes, and experiences, and to identify applicants most likely to thrive and contribute to this mission. Aspects considered include academic performance, breadth and depth of life experiences, and personal attributes gauged through the written application, letters of recommendation, and interview performance.
